change_second_slice.what: a destination whose resolved contributions are all variable-free resolves them in order, compares the signature with the last folded one, and restores the stored aggregate on a hit; opens no side-effect risk because merging closed terms binds no variables
change_second_slice.why_sound: merges of closed terms are pure term construction, so resolving all contributions before merging is equivalent to the interleaved order used for mixed folds; mixed folds keep the interleaved path and are never memoized

findings: NovyWave's refresh cost is almost entirely merge_type_evidence: 189.8 ms over 119,920 variable-bearing merges, about 1.6 us each. Closed-pair caching cannot help: only 639 of those merges are between closed terms.

TodoMVC's merge work is trivial (16.7 ms over 44,262 merges); its refresh cost sits in invalidation (86.9 ms per the reviewer), commit/order (68.1 ms) and assembly (31.2 ms), with 85.8% of refresh calls carrying an empty dirty queue.
Closed-merge pairs are cacheable in principle but small: TodoMVC 3,753 closed merges over 78 distinct pairs (3,675 hits), NovyWave 639 over 131 pairs.
